title: EP-PQC-001 — Pre-Execution Post-Quantum Cryptographic Policy Verification (an ExecutionProof experiment)
description:
EP-PQC-001 is a software-only ExecutionProof™ research experiment. It tests whether a pre-execution verification gateway can physically block a cryptographic operation from crossing an execution boundary when the system cannot independently prove that the operation satisfies a defined post-quantum cryptography (PQC) policy. The gateway does not trust labels: for each request it re-derives the true algorithm family from the raw key bytes (DER parsing for classical RSA/ECDH; exact FIPS-203 byte-lengths plus a functional encapsulation probe for ML-KEM), recomputes artifact hashes, verifies a real ML-DSA-65 evidence-manifest signature, and enforces authority, freshness, binding, nonce single-use, and policy constraints. The protected ML-KEM encapsulation runs only on ALLOW.

Results (preserved verbatim): the root run EP-PQC-001 (24 cases) is PARTIAL / safety-PASS — decision 23/24, reason 22/24, zero false ALLOW, no safety-invariant violations, with two SAFE classification deviations (PQC-04, PQC-12) traced to test design rather than the enforcement engine. The remediation run EP-PQC-001R1 (26 cases), using the byte-identical engine with only the test design corrected, is a clean PASS (26/26 decision, 26/26 reason, zero false ALLOW).

Limitations: this is a bounded software simulation. It does not claim CNSA 2.0 compliance, NIST certification, quantum resistance of ExecutionProof, production or defense readiness, HSM/TPM/live-TLS validation, or third-party validation, and it does not prove the security of ML-KEM or ML-DSA. Policy profiles are experimental, not compliance controls. Blinding is procedural (single author).
notes: License: Apache-2.0 for source code; CC-BY-4.0 for documentation and data. One disclosed, non-fatal erratum: R1/proofrecords/proofrecord_PQC-17b.json carries an internal request_id of 'PQC-17a' (a generator typo); the record is otherwise correct (decision HOLD, reason EVID_NONCE_REPLAY) and its record_hash matches the frozen raw_decisions.json row for PQC-17b exactly. The frozen artifact was intentionally NOT modified, because editing a sealed ProofRecord would change its record_hash and break the evidence chain. See ERRATA.md. All ProofRecords self-verify via the standalone verify_proofrecords.py and reconcile against a consolidated HASHES.txt manifest.
